pattern: Single-plugin layered architecture following RuneLite's standard external-plugin shape: a Guice-injected Plugin class as orchestrator/controller, a dedicated HTTP API client layer, a Gson DTO layer mirroring the backend's JSON contract, and a Swing view layer (state-routed panel + presentational cards + a custom widget kit). Not MVC/MVVM in a strict sense - closer to a thin controller (the Plugin class) pushing state into a stateful, self-rendering View (CatastrophicEventsPanel).

layers.name: Plugin entrypoint / orchestrator
layers.responsibility: Guice lifecycle (startUp/shutDown), schedules the 45s poll loop, drives reminder-milestone logic, wires the panel's join-button callback to the API client, routes API results/errors into panel state transitions

layers.name: Config
layers.responsibility: RuneLite ConfigGroup interface declaring the plugin's user-facing settings (token, apiBase, websiteBase, guildId) with defaults, surfaced both in RuneLite's standard config UI and in the plugin's own inline SettingsView

layers.name: API client
layers.responsibility: EventsApiClient wraps OkHttp calls to the bot's plugin API (GET /events, POST /signup); ApiCallback<T> is the async result interface; ApiErrorType classifies failures (UNAUTHORIZED / NETWORK / SERVER) so callers can branch on cause

layers.name: DTOs
layers.responsibility: Gson-deserialized shapes matching the bot's plugin API JSON exactly (EventDto, EventsResponse, SignupRequest, SignupResponse); ids are Strings because they're Mongo ObjectIds on the backend

layers.name: UI / View
layers.responsibility: CatastrophicEventsPanel is the top-level state machine (NOT_LINKED / CONNECTION_ERROR / EVENTS) and tab router (All Events / My Events); EventHeroCard and EventCompactRow are presentational cards; SettingsView is the inline config form; StyledButton, CircleIconButton, PillBadge, RoundedPanel, WrappingLabel, AvatarIcon, CatastrophicTheme form a small custom-painted widget kit (gold-on-black theme, no default Swing L&F chrome)

layers.name: Dev launcher
layers.responsibility: Boots a full RuneLite client in developer mode with the plugin preloaded, for manual local testing via `./gradlew run` - not an automated test despite living under src/test

key_patterns: Dependency Injection via Guice (RuneLite's plugin framework) - @Inject fields, @Provides for CatastrophicEventsConfig
Async callback interface for HTTP results (ApiCallback<T>), wrapping OkHttp's own Callback
Explicit state machine driving a full re-render (CatastrophicEventsPanel.State enum; render() rebuilds the entire body panel on every state/tab change rather than diffing)
DTO/contract isolation - api/dto package exists solely to mirror the bot's JSON shape, translated via Gson @SerializedName, kept separate from UI/domain logic
Composable custom Swing widget kit instead of the platform look-and-feel

key_decisions.decision: Reminders are private and client-side only, rendered via ChatMessageManager - nothing is sent to the game server or the backend
key_decisions.reason: No rate-limit or game-integrity concerns apply since it's purely local rendering; documented explicitly in poc-runelite-plugin.md
key_decisions.made_at: unknown (pre-dates this repo's git history - carried over from the original POC design doc)

key_decisions.decision: The plugin token is stored in RuneLite's local ConfigManager, UI-masked (secret=true) but not otherwise encrypted
key_decisions.reason: Same trust model as any other plugin credential - local to the user's own machine

key_decisions.decision: Discord deep-link and the website's 'View Event' page are opened via Desktop.browse() (OS-level action), not rendered in-panel
key_decisions.reason: No automation caution applies to opening the user's own default browser

key_decisions.decision: Auto check-in, drop-screenshot capture, join-VC, and LFC browsing are out of scope for this POC but shown as visible, disabled 'Coming soon' rows in the My Events hero card rather than hidden entirely
key_decisions.reason: The mocked-up design the panel was built against calls for them to be visible
